title: Liverpool Sells Stake to Bezos-Backed Consortium Led by British-Indian Businessman Amit Bhatia
excerpt: A group including Amazon's Jeff Bezos and the Mittal family will acquire roughly 30% of Liverpool FC in a deal valuing the club at £5.5 billion, with Bhatia becoming vice-chairman.
body:
• Fenway Sports Group has sold approximately one-third of Liverpool FC to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia and backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.
  • The deal is worth roughly £1.65 billion, valuing Liverpool at approximately £5.5 billion — a massive increase from FSG's £300 million acquisition in 2010.
  • Bhatia will become Liverpool's vice-chairman and join an expanded board, while FSG retains majority ownership and operational control.
  • The transaction is subject to approval from the Independent Football Regulator and the Premier League's owners' and directors' test.

Liverpool FC has a new set of minority stakeholders — and they include some of the wealthiest people on the planet. Fenway Sports Group confirmed Friday that it has reached a definitive agreement to sell approximately 30% of the club to a consortium called 1892 Holdings, led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia.

The Consortium

The investor group brings together a striking collection of global wealth. Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, stepped down from the board at Championship club Queens Park Rangers last month, ending an 18-year association and transferring his stake to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam to avoid any conflict of interest.

https://x.com/FansTribeHQ/status/2088328919111856638

Alongside Bhatia, the consortium includes the Mittal Family Trusts, EE Capital (represented by Elaine Saverin, wife of Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin), and K5 Sports, where Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is the lead investor. Forbes lists Bezos as the third-richest person in the world with a net worth exceeding $270 billion. This is his first known investment in a sports team, though he had previously explored bids for NFL franchises including the Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders.

"To be welcomed as a partner in a club of this stature is a huge privilege. We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership."

— Amit Bhatia, Chairman of 1892 Holdings

The Deal

The transaction is worth approximately £1.65 billion, according to The Times, valuing Liverpool at roughly £5.5 billion. FSG acquired the club for £300 million in 2010, meaning its value has increased more than eighteen-fold in 16 years. The BBC reported the valuation at between £5-6 billion, while earlier estimates from the Financial Times had placed it above $6 billion.

FSG will retain majority ownership and operational control of the club. The deal is not a direct capital raise for Liverpool and does not signal a change in transfer strategy, though the transaction documents provide options for a deeper relationship over time. Bhatia will become vice-chairman and take a seat on an expanded board, alongside Elaine Saverin and Bryan Baum, who represents Bezos's K5 Sports fund. Bezos himself will not join the board.

Liverpool's Position

Liverpool announced record revenues of £703 million in its last accounting period and has spent approximately £550 million on new signings over the past 14 months. The club was not seeking investment out of financial necessity, according to people familiar with the deal. FSG believes the opportunity was notable because of the calibre of the investors involved and the relationships they bring.

"As we considered this opportunity, it became clear that Amit and the consortium shared our long-term philosophy and appreciation for what makes Liverpool special," FSG president Mike Gordon said in a statement.

On-Field Transition

The investment comes during a period of on-field transition. Liverpool won the Premier League title in 2024-25 under Arne Slot but struggled to repeat the feat last season, finishing fifth. Slot has since departed, replaced by Andoni Iraola. Prolific forward Mohamed Salah has also left, and Michael Edwards, the CEO of football at FSG widely credited with building Liverpool's title-winning squad, stepped down in July.

The deal is subject to approval from the new Independent Football Regulator and the Premier League's owners' and directors' test, which could take up to 90 days. The new season begins with Liverpool traveling to Newcastle United on August 23.

Indian Connection

The deal puts a British-Indian businessman at the helm of one of English football's most storied clubs. Bhatia, 46, has deep roots in both the Indian business world through the Mittal family and in English football through his nearly two-decade involvement with QPR. The Mittal Family Trusts' participation adds another layer to the growing presence of Indian capital in global sports ownership, joining the likes of the Ambani family's involvement in the Indian Premier League and Indian Super League.
